statement: Writing vals(l) for the sequence of values stored in the nodes of list l from head to tail, whenever the function returns a result r, vals(r) = distinct(vals(head)), where distinct(s) is the sequence obtained from s by keeping the first occurrence of each value and deleting all later occurrences of that value. Because the input is sorted nondecreasing, this is equivalently the strictly increasing sequence of the distinct values occurring in head.
preconditions: Let n = len(head). Assume 0 <= n <= 300. For every i with 0 <= i < n, the value of the i-th node of head (0-based) is between -100 and 100 inclusive. For every i with 0 <= i < n-1, head[i] <= head[i+1] (the list is sorted nondecreasing; equal adjacent values are duplicates).

statement: The function returns a result r (it does not fail) for every input satisfying the preconditions.
preconditions: Let n = len(head). Assume 0 <= n <= 300. For every i with 0 <= i < n, the value of the i-th node of head (0-based) is between -100 and 100 inclusive. For every i with 0 <= i < n-1, head[i] <= head[i+1] (the list is sorted nondecreasing; equal adjacent values are duplicates).

statement: Writing vals(l) for the sequence of values in l, whenever the function returns a result r, vals(r) is a subsequence of vals(head): there is a strictly increasing sequence of indices j_0 < j_1 < ... < j_{m-1} with m = len(r) and 0 <= j_k < len(head) for all k, such that r[k] = head[j_k] for every k with 0 <= k < m. (When m = 0 the sequence of indices is empty.)
preconditions: Let n = len(head). Assume 0 <= n <= 300. For every i with 0 <= i < n, the value of the i-th node of head (0-based) is between -100 and 100 inclusive. For every i with 0 <= i < n-1, head[i] <= head[i+1] (the list is sorted nondecreasing; equal adjacent values are duplicates).

statement: Writing vals(l) for the sequence of values in l, whenever the function returns a result r, for every i with 0 <= i < len(r)-1, r[i] < r[i+1].
preconditions: Let n = len(head). Assume 0 <= n <= 300. For every i with 0 <= i < n, the value of the i-th node of head (0-based) is between -100 and 100 inclusive. For every i with 0 <= i < n-1, head[i] <= head[i+1] (the list is sorted nondecreasing; equal adjacent values are duplicates).

statement: Writing occurs(v, l) to mean that some node of l has value v (i.e. there is i with 0 <= i < len(l) and the i-th node value of l equals v), whenever the function returns a result r, for every i64 v, occurs(v, r) iff occurs(v, head).
preconditions: Let n = len(head). Assume 0 <= n <= 300. For every i with 0 <= i < n, the value of the i-th node of head (0-based) is between -100 and 100 inclusive. For every i with 0 <= i < n-1, head[i] <= head[i+1] (the list is sorted nondecreasing; equal adjacent values are duplicates).

statement: Writing vals(l) for the sequence of values in l, whenever the function returns a result r, if len(head) > 0 then len(r) > 0 and r[0] = head[0].
preconditions: Let n = len(head). Assume 0 <= n <= 300. For every i with 0 <= i < n, the value of the i-th node of head (0-based) is between -100 and 100 inclusive. For every i with 0 <= i < n-1, head[i] <= head[i+1] (the list is sorted nondecreasing; equal adjacent values are duplicates).

statement: Writing vals(l) for the sequence of values in l, whenever the function returns a result r, if len(head) > 0 then len(r) > 0 and r[len(r)-1] = head[len(head)-1].
preconditions: Let n = len(head). Assume 0 <= n <= 300. For every i with 0 <= i < n, the value of the i-th node of head (0-based) is between -100 and 100 inclusive. For every i with 0 <= i < n-1, head[i] <= head[i+1] (the list is sorted nondecreasing; equal adjacent values are duplicates).

statement: Writing vals(l) for the sequence of values in l and len(l) for its length, whenever the function returns a result r, len(r) equals the number of indices i such that 0 <= i < len(head) and (i = 0 or head[i] > head[i-1]).
preconditions: Let n = len(head). Assume 0 <= n <= 300. For every i with 0 <= i < n, the value of the i-th node of head (0-based) is between -100 and 100 inclusive. For every i with 0 <= i < n-1, head[i] <= head[i+1] (the list is sorted nondecreasing; equal adjacent values are duplicates).

statement: Writing vals(l) for the sequence of values in l, whenever the function returns a result r, for every i with 0 <= i < len(r), -100 <= r[i] <= 100.
